candidates.source_name: Uprava policije – Sektor za finansijsko-obavještajne poslove (FIU Montenegro) – official site
candidates.why_relevant: Montenegro's Financial Intelligence Unit (formerly Uprava za sprječavanje pranja novca i finansiranja terorizma, now a sector of the Police Administration) is the primary AML/CFT authority for obliged entities including banks, payment institutions and e-money issuers. Its site carries news, the legal framework, sanctions-list updates and the 'ZA OBVEZNIKE' section that drives reporting duties.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scheduled HTML crawl of /foj sub-pages plus /vijesti?sort=published_at listing; diff for new items
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search + direct fetch of institution site
queries_used: Uprava za sprječavanje pranja novca i finansiranja terorizma Crna Gora sajt upn.gov.me
Montenegro AML CFT directorate guidance obliged entities deadline

candidates.source_name: FIU Montenegro – 'Za obveznike' (obliged entities) page
candidates.why_relevant: Operational compliance hub: electronic reporting of cash, suspicious and other transactions; table of activity codes for obliged entities under Art. 4(2)(13) of the AML/CFT Law; ML/TF typologies; beneficial-owner identification instructions. This is where reporting obligations and formats for banks/payment firms are set out.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Page fetch + PDF/attachment harvest, content-hash diff on change
queries_used: Uprava za sprječavanje pranja novca Crna Gora smjernice obveznici

candidates.source_name: Vlada Crne Gore – dokumenta repository (FIU/AML documents)
candidates.why_relevant: Central government document repository where FIU/ministry AML reports, forms, EU Council sanctions decisions and strategy documents are deposited. Acts as a pointer to authoritative PDFs that are not always linked from institutional landing pages.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Keyword-filtered crawl of the documents index (terms: pranje novca, obveznici, smjernice, nacrt zakona)
queries_used: Uprava za sprječavanje pranja novca i finansiranja terorizma Crna Gora sajt upn.gov.me

candidates.source_name: Komisija za tržište kapitala Crne Gore (Capital Market Authority) – official site
candidates.why_relevant: Independent securities/capital-market regulator (IOSCO/ESMA-aligned). Publishes regulations (Regulativa), forms, warnings about unlicensed operators, market-participant registers, and news. Directly relevant to banks with investment services, custody, fund business and to payment firms crossing into investment services.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl /me/regulativa, /me/novosti, /me/upozorenja on a weekly cadence; harvest PDFs under /images/files/
queries_used: Komisija za tržište kapitala Crna Gora propisi

candidates.source_name: Komisija za tržište kapitala – javne rasprave / nacrti pravila (draft rules consultations)
candidates.why_relevant: Consultation drafts of subordinate rules are posted as dated PDF folders (e.g. 'Nacrti-pravila-26.02.2026'). This is the earliest visible signal of forthcoming capital-market obligations and their comment deadlines.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monitor the news page for 'javna rasprava' items and follow to the dated PDF folder; directory listing may not be browsable, so follow links rather than guessing paths
queries_used: Komisija za tržište kapitala Crna Gora propisi

candidates.source_name: Komisija za tržište kapitala – SPNFT (AML/CFT) section
candidates.why_relevant: The capital market authority is itself an AML/CFT supervisor for its licensees; this section carries its own AML guidance and supervisory expectations, separate from the CBCG and FIU streams.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Page fetch with change detection; also fetch the /me/ Montenegrin equivalent
queries_used: Uprava za sprječavanje pranja novca i finansiranja terorizma Crna Gora sajt upn.gov.me
local_language_terms_used: sprječavanje pranja novca i finansiranja terorizma

candidates.source_name: Centralni registar propisanih informacija (CRPI) – Capital Market Authority
candidates.why_relevant: Officially designated central registry of regulated/prescribed disclosures by issuers (transparency-directive style). Useful as a structured feed of mandatory issuer disclosures, including those of listed Montenegrin banks.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Locate the CRPI entry link from the scmn.me homepage (exact deep URL not confirmed in this pass), then structured scrape of the disclosure listing
queries_used: Komisija za tržište kapitala Crna Gora propisi

candidates.source_name: Agencija za zaštitu ličnih podataka i slobodan pristup informacijama (AZLP) – official site
candidates.why_relevant: Montenegro's DPA. Publishes opinions (mišljenja), recommendations (preporuke), supervisory decisions (rješenja), registries of data collections, forms and annual reports. Banks and payment firms face direct obligations here (video surveillance, direct marketing, biometrics, cross-border transfers, breach handling) and inspection findings against named controllers are published.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl /me/zastita-licnih-podataka subtree and /me/preporuke; harvest .doc/.pdf decisions under /storage/docs/ and /docs/
queries_used: Agencija za zaštitu ličnih podataka Crna Gora smjernice banke
Agencija za zaštitu ličnih podataka Crna Gora azlp.me smjernice

candidates.source_name: AZLP – supervisory decisions archive (rješenja, by year)
candidates.why_relevant: Year-foldered archive of individual supervisory decisions naming controllers, including public bodies and companies. High-value for tracking enforcement patterns and what the DPA actually penalises — a leading indicator of compliance risk for financial-sector controllers.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Follow links from the decisions index page rather than assuming directory listing; note the site uses both /docs/ and /storage/docs/ path prefixes (legacy vs current)
candidates.discovered_via_method: URL pattern observed in search results
queries_used: Agencija za zaštitu ličnih podataka Crna Gora azlp.me smjernice
local_language_terms_used: izvještaj o stanju zaštite ličnih podataka

candidates.source_name: Agencija za nadzor osiguranja (ANO) – Insurance Supervision Agency
candidates.why_relevant: Prudential and conduct supervisor for insurers, insurance agents and brokers since 2007. Relevant to banks via bancassurance distribution, to payment firms via embedded insurance, and it operates its own AML/CFT obligations page and consumer-complaint channel. Sections: Regulativa, Statistika i izvještavanje, Publikacije, Prigovori i zaštita potrošača.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Weekly crawl of /zakoni/, /izvjestaji/, /tematski-bilteni, /prigovori-i-zastita-potrosaca/
queries_used: Agencija za nadzor osiguranja Crna Gora ano.me nadzor osiguranja 2026

candidates.source_name: ANO – AML/CFT obligations page for insurance obliged entities
candidates.why_relevant: Sets out how the AML/CFT Law applies to insurance-sector obliged entities under ANO supervision — a compliance stream distinct from CBCG and FIU guidance and easily missed if 'the regulator' is treated as one body.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Page fetch; note the legacy Joomla query-string URL may be superseded by a clean-URL equivalent on the new ano.me site
queries_used: Uprava za sprječavanje pranja novca Crna Gora smjernice obveznici
local_language_terms_used: Zakon o sprječavanju pranja novca i finansiranja terorizma

candidates.source_name: Uprava za inspekcijske poslove – Tržišna inspekcija (Market Inspection)
candidates.why_relevant: The inspection authority whose Market Inspection department enforces the Consumer Protection Law, including consumers' economic interests, advertising of products and services, and consumer complaints. It publishes annual work reports and work programmes that reveal inspection priorities and complaint volumes touching financial services.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Annual harvest of Izvještaj o radu and Program rada PDFs (served from wapi.gov.me download endpoints) plus news monitoring
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search on consumer protection enforcement

candidates.source_name: eKonsultacije / e-participacija (eUprava) – national public consultation portal
candidates.why_relevant: Single national platform where draft laws and bylaws are posted for public consultation (minimum 15 days, often 24-40). Consultations relevant to this cell (AML law amendments, consumer protection law, financial conglomerates, tax dispute mechanisms) surface here with explicit comment deadlines.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Daily/weekly listing scrape filtered on keywords (banka, platni promet, pranje novca, potrošač, lični podaci); capture consultation open/close dates
queries_used: ekonsultacije.gov.me javna rasprava nacrt zakona Crna Gora

candidates.source_name: Ministarstvo finansija – Javne rasprave (public consultations)
candidates.why_relevant: The Ministry of Finance is the sponsor of most financial-sector legislation (AML/CFT law, financial conglomerates, tax mechanisms). Its consultations page carries drafts and deadlines before they reach the regulators' implementing acts. Note: the ministry appears under both mif.gov.me and gov.me article URLs — track both.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Weekly crawl of the consultations listing plus gov.me article search for 'javna rasprava' + 'nacrt zakona'
queries_used: ekonsultacije.gov.me javna rasprava nacrt zakona Crna Gora

candidates.source_name: Službeni list Crne Gore (Official Gazette) – free digitally signed electronic edition
candidates.why_relevant: Authoritative point of legal effect: every law, bylaw, regulator rulebook and its entry-into-force/transition deadline is published here. The electronic edition is free and digitally signed. Separate editions exist for international treaties and municipal regulations.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Poll the issue index (aktuelnosti) for new numbered issues; parse the table of contents for financial-sector acts and extract in-force dates
queries_used: Službeni list Crne Gore sluzbenilist.me elektronsko izdanje propisi

candidates.source_name: PropisiNet.me / Paragraf.me – commercial consolidated Montenegrin legislation databases
candidates.why_relevant: Commercial aggregators that publish consolidated texts of Montenegrin laws (Consumer Protection Law, Anti-Corruption Law, capital market bills) and issue-by-issue Official Gazette summaries, often faster and more navigable than the gazette itself. Useful as a cross-check and for consolidated text, not as the legal source of record.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Metadata/headline monitoring only (issue numbers, act titles); do not mirror full consolidated texts — likely subject to copyright and subscription terms
queries_used: Službeni list Crne Gore sluzbenilist.me elektronsko izdanje propisi
Komisija za tržište kapitala Crna Gora propisi

candidates.source_name: Agencija za sprječavanje korupcije (ASK) – anti-corruption agency and public registers
candidates.why_relevant: Integrity body maintaining public registers of officials' income/asset declarations, conflicts of interest, lobbyists and gift records. These registers are the practical domestic source for PEP identification and enhanced due diligence by Montenegrin banks, and ASK also issues integrity-plan and whistleblowing guidance.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Structured scrape of the registri pages; check for bulk/open-data export before crawling record-by-record. Personal data — restrict use to lawful PEP/DD purposes

candidates.source_name: MONEYVAL (Council of Europe) – Montenegro country page and follow-up reports
candidates.why_relevant: Montenegro's 5th-round MER was adopted December 2023 and it remains in enhanced follow-up, with follow-up reports adopted at the 70th Plenary (Dec 2025) and a further report due within a year. These reports are the single best forward-looking indicator of what Montenegrin AML supervisors will demand of banks and payment firms next.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monitor plenary outcome pages and the Montenegro country/publications page; mirror the FUR PDFs (also mirrored on fatf-gafi.org)
candidates.discovered_via_method: English-language search on international AML assessment

candidates.source_name: CEZAP – Centar za zaštitu potrošača Crne Gore (consumer protection NGO)
candidates.why_relevant: The main Montenegrin consumer NGO (est. 1999), an active participant in drafting the Consumer Protection Law under which banking, credit, insurance, investment and payment-transaction services are classified as financial services. Its news and campaigns reveal consumer complaint themes and pending regulatory pressure on banks before authorities act.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: RSS/news scrape of cezap.me; note a legacy domain cezap.org also carries a Novosti archive

candidates.why_relevant: Non-CBCG authority imposing reporting duties directly on Montenegrin financial institutions: the FATCA agreement with the US has been in force since 2018 and AEOI/CRS implementation has been repeatedly delayed. Any CRS go-live decision creates hard reporting deadlines for banks. Coverage is thin and needs manual confirmation.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Confirm the current canonical URL for the authority on gov.me (the body has been reorganised/renamed), then monitor news and instruction pages for FATCA/CRS notices

candidates.why_relevant: Specialist local-language outlet covering the insurance supervisor, consumer protection in banking and regulatory developments, with topic tag pages per institution. negative_findings.description: The standalone 'Uprava za sprječavanje pranja novca i finansiranja terorizma' with a presumed domain upn.gov.me could not be found as a live independent site. All current evidence points to the function having been absorbed into the Police Administration as the 'Sektor za finansijsko-obavještajne poslove' at gov.me/foj.
negative_findings.result_summary: No upn.gov.me page surfaced in either local-language or English searching; gov.me/foj resolved and returned a full navigation.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A collection plan keyed to the old directorate name or a guessed upn.gov.me domain would silently collect nothing. The FIU must be tracked under gov.me/foj and under 'finansijsko-obavještajni' terminology, not only under 'Uprava za sprječavanje pranja novca'.

negative_findings.description: The FIU site (gov.me/foj) exposes news, legal framework, obliged-entity and sanctions pages, but no discrete 'Smjernice' (guidance) or 'Izvještaji' (reports) section was visible in navigation. The obliged-entities page links out to CBCG for beneficial-owner instructions.
negative_findings.result_summary: Navigation enumerated; guidance appears dispersed across the obliged-entities page, gov.me/dokumenta and CBCG rather than centralised.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: AML guidance for Montenegro cannot be collected from one FIU URL; a multi-target harvest (FIU obveznici page + gov.me/dokumenta + CBCG + ANO + KTK) is required, otherwise guidance will appear absent.

negative_findings.description: https://www.azlp.me/me/ returned HTTP 404 on fetch, while https://www.azlp.me/me/preporuke fetched successfully and revealed the full navigation.
negative_findings.result_summary: 404 on the assumed locale root; sibling paths live. Treated as a routing quirk, not a dead site.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A crawler seeded on the /me/ root would report the DPA as unreachable. Seeds must point at real section paths (/me/preporuke, /me/zastita-licnih-podataka) or the bare domain.

negative_findings.description: Three distinct consultation surfaces appeared: euprava.gov.me/e-participacija (state), ekonsultacije.epodgorica.me (Podgorica municipality), and per-ministry javne rasprave pages. The generic 'ekonsultacije.gov.me' host named in the seed framing was not directly confirmed.
negative_findings.result_summary: State consultations confirmed on euprava.gov.me/e-participacija and on ministry pages; the municipal eKonsultacije platform is a different, local-government scope.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Seeding the municipal portal would produce irrelevant Podgorica planning consultations and miss national financial-sector drafts.

negative_findings.description: No Montenegrin-language term or dedicated institution was found for a financial-services ombudsman or an out-of-court ADR body for banking disputes outside the CBCG. Consumer redress paths located were: ANO's prigovori channel (insurance), the Market Inspection (general consumer protection), and CEZAP (NGO).
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches in Montenegrin on consumer protection in financial services returned only the general Consumer Protection Law framework, the inspectorate and the NGO.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: If such a body exists under a name I did not guess, complaint-level intelligence on banks and payment firms is being missed. Needs a targeted follow-up on the Consumer Protection Law text for named redress bodies.

negative_findings.description: Montenegro's CRS/AEOI status is contradictory across sources: one source suggests AEOI-standard exchange as of January 2026, another states Montenegro failed to meet CRS MCAA requirements and lacks the necessary IT system. FATCA in force since 2018 is the only firm fact.
negative_findings.result_summary: No authoritative Montenegrin tax-authority page confirming CRS reporting obligations or deadlines for financial institutions was located.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: CRS go-live would create hard, dated reporting obligations for every Montenegrin bank. The status must be resolved against the tax authority and the OECD AEOI portal before it can be used.

negative_findings.description: Local-language AML queries are heavily contaminated by Croatian and Serbian results (mfin.gov.hr, hgk.hr, paragraf.rs, KPMG Serbia) because the terminology is near-identical across the region ('sprječavanje/sprečavanje pranja novca', 'obveznici', 'smjernice').
negative_findings.result_summary: Roughly half of first-page results on the seed AML query were non-Montenegrin.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Automated collection keyed on these terms without a .me / 'Crna Gora' constraint will ingest the wrong jurisdiction's rules — a serious correctness risk for a compliance-deadline product.

negative_findings.description: Several bodies serve content from two path/domain generations simultaneously: azlp.me uses both /docs/ and /storage/docs/; ano.me uses both clean URLs and legacy Joomla index.php query strings; cezap.me coexists with cezap.org.
negative_findings.result_summary: Live documents observed on both variants for AZLP and ANO.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Deduplication and link-rot handling must treat these as the same source; a naive crawler will either double-count or drop the legacy archive, which holds the older decisions and guidance.

coverage_gaps.description: No source located for a securities/investor-compensation fund, a deposit protection body outside CBCG scope, or the Central Depository Agency (CDA/Centralna klirinško depozitarna društva) whose rulebooks bind banks acting as custodians — the T+1 settlement change from 1 January 2027 implies such rulebooks exist.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search 'Centralna depozitarna agencija Crna Gora', 'CKB depozitarna', 'Montenegroberza', 'T+1 saldiranje pravila' and follow from the Capital Market Authority's učesnici-na-trzistu register.

coverage_gaps.description: None of the cell's regulators (FIU, KTK, AZLP, ANO, UIP) were confirmed to offer RSS, an API, or an open-data export. All appear to require HTML scraping and PDF harvesting.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Probe each site for /feed, /rss, sitemap.xml and robots.txt before designing the collector; budget for PDF text extraction and for Cyrillic/Latin plus diacritic normalisation (č, ć, š, ž, đ) in matching.

coverage_gaps.description: Consultation and in-force deadlines are expressed in prose inside Montenegrin-language PDFs and news items ('javna rasprava traje 24 dana', 'od 1. januara 2027'), not in structured fields anywhere in this cell.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a Montenegrin date/duration extraction rule set (month names in the locative, 'traje X dana', 'stupa na snagu', 'rok za dostavljanje primjedbi') and validate it against the confirmed examples in this slice.

coverage_gaps.description: English coverage of these non-central-bank bodies is very thin: only the Capital Market Authority and MONEYVAL offered substantive English pages. AZLP, the FIU and the inspectorate are effectively Montenegrin-only.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Treat Montenegrin as the mandatory primary collection language for this cell and plan machine translation downstream rather than relying on English mirrors, which lag or do not exist.

coverage_gaps.description: Inspection findings and sanctions imposed on banks and payment firms by these non-CBCG bodies were not located in any consolidated form; AZLP publishes individual rješenja and UIP publishes aggregate annual reports, but there is no per-entity enforcement register.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Establish whether AZLP and UIP publish a sanctions/misdemeanour register, and consider the misdemeanour courts (Sud za prekršaje) as an indirect source of published penalty decisions.

coverage_gaps.description: The Skupština Crne Gore (Parliament) pipeline — bill tabling, committee stage, adopted texts — was not sourced in this pass, though a Predlog zakona o tržištu kapitala PDF surfaced indirectly via a commercial aggregator.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add skupstina.me bill tracking as a distinct pointer source; it sits between the ministry consultation stage and the Official Gazette and carries the firmest pre-enactment timing signal.

brief: Montenegro's non-CBCG compliance perimeter for banks and payment firms is set by at least six separate bodies: the FIU (now the Police Administration's Sektor za finansijsko-obavještajne poslove at gov.me/foj, not the presumed standalone upn.gov.me directorate), the Capital Market Authority (scmn.me), the data protection authority AZLP (azlp.me), the Insurance Supervision Agency (ano.me), the Market Inspection within Uprava za inspekcijske poslove, and the anti-corruption agency ASK whose public registers underpin domestic PEP screening. Each publishes its own rules, guidance and consultation drafts on its own site with no common feed, no machine-readable export identified, and material content almost exclusively in Montenegrin; the only convergence points are the Official Gazette (sluzbenilist.me, free and digitally signed) for legal effect and euprava.gov.me/e-participacija plus ministry pages for consultation deadlines. The dominant risks for a collector are jurisdictional contamination — regional terminology pulls in Croatian and Serbian rules on identical search terms — and institutional renaming, which has already orphaned the old AML directorate name. Forward-looking pressure is best read from MONEYVAL, which keeps Montenegro in enhanced follow-up with a further progress report due after the December 2025 plenary.
